sources.entry: Apprise - Apprise allows you to send a notification to almost all of the most popular notification services available to us today such as: Telegram, Discord, Slack, Amazon SNS, Gotify, etc. MIT Python/Docker/deb

summary.one_liner: Apprise is a Python notification library and `apprise` CLI that sends messages to a very large number of services (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Amazon SNS, Gotify, email and more) using one URL format.
summary.what_it_does: Apprise takes a single consistent URL syntax for each notification service and provides a common notification interface for scripts, apps, and infrastructure. The README documents support for productivity chat tools, SMS providers, desktop notifications (DBus, GNOME, macOS, Windows), email via mailto/mailtos, and generic Form, JSON and XML POST targets. It can be used as a Python library, through the `apprise` command line tool reading stdin or a body argument, or by relaying through Apprise API. Messages can include file attachments where the destination service accepts them. Configuration can be kept in YAML or TEXT files loaded from default paths or over HTTP, with tags for grouping, priority-based escalation, and per-call retries. YAML configs also support `${NAME}` template variables filled from CLI flags or environment variables.
use_cases: send server alerts to chat channels
send notifications from shell scripts or cron jobs
pipe command output to a phone or chat app
add notifications to a Python application
route alerts to several services by tag
notable: One URL format covers a very large set of notification services, documented in tables by category
CLI tool and core library share the same service URLs
Tag-based routing with OR/AND logic and priority escalation chains
Custom notification hooks via an @notify decorator
Template variables let YAML configs keep secrets out of version control
caveats: Support is described as 'almost' all popular services, so some may be missing
Some services need extra setup such as accounts, API keys, or self-hosted servers
Attachments only work with services that accept them
